title: Folder parents are checked and deletes lock against filing
folder:delete checks assignment hosts in batches
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate` in apps that mount folders and apply the migration that adds the index.

title: Folder tree and picker no longer stop silently at 50 folders
Folder tree helpers on the server-neutral folders entry
Prebuilt folder handler constants removed
detail: `setFolderHandler` and `clearFolderHandler` are no longer exported from the folders feature. They were default-access copies of `createSetFolderHandler` and `createClearFolderHandler`, which stay; the feature mounts the factories with its host list and the assignment executor.
migration: Do not register `setFolderHandler` or `clearFolderHandler` yourself; mount `createFoldersFeature({ parents })`. A custom feature that needs the handler calls `createSetFolderHandler(access, assignmentExecutor)` or `createClearFolderHandler(access, assignmentExecutor)`.

title: Folder assignments enforce ownership.write
detail: createFoldersFeature({ ownership: { write } }) now gates set-folder (create, move, restore) and clear-folder like the tags feature does. Before, the handlers wrote through an executor without the rule, so any caller with handler access could file or unfile another user's records.
migration: Direct callers of createFolderAssignmentExecutor pass the ownership option first: createFolderAssignmentExecutor(ownership, parents).

title: The deprecated foldersFeature constant is removed
detail: foldersFeature was kept next to createFoldersFeature() for one release. Mount the feature by calling createFoldersFeature().
migration: Run bun kumiko-upgrade --apply. It replaces foldersFeature with createFoldersFeature().

title: folder:delete removes assignments whose host entity is gone instead of refusing forever
set-folder and clear-folder now verify entityType/entityId against the host entity's own read path
migration: entityType must now name an entity registered in the same app (via r.entity(...) or a bundled feature), and the caller must be able to see the target row through that entity's own read path. Any consumer that called set-folder or clear-folder with an entityType that is NOT a registered entity name, or with an entityId the caller could not otherwise read, will now get a not_found error instead of a successful write — register the host entity (and, if it needs row-level ownership, its `access.read` rule) before upgrading. Note the consequence for hard-deleted host rows: once the host row is gone, its folder-assignment can no longer be cleared, and folder:delete keeps refusing while that assignment points at the folder.
